category: debrid link generator with torrent and usenet backends

free_tier.stated: No free allowance on this plan; it is the US$3/month entry tier. The free plan is a separate record.

per_object_cap.notes: The API error table gives the same limit as 214748364800 bytes, which is 200 GiB; the pricing page says 200GB. The GiB reading is the larger of the two, so 200 GB is the conservative figure.

retention.stated: 300 GB of permanent storage (AirLock) plus 24-hour seeding time
retention.notes: Seeding stops after 24 hours; the file stays cached and downloadable.

egress.terms: 'Unlimited Downloads' on the plan, subject to the terms' fair-use clause and the three active slots. No byte allowance is published for the month.

interface_detail: REST API with a bearer API key; the vendor documents 300 requests a minute per token with separate hourly caps on uncached torrent, usenet and web-download creation.
tooling: Documented API, Postman collection, third-party media-server integrations. Torrents, magnets, NZB and web downloads share one API surface.
chaining: The cheapest paid tier that removes the free plan's download counter; it is the tier to test usenet against because it does not exist on Free, but the support article says usenet starts at Pro, so a user would be paying for torrents alone here.

limits.value: three active downloads or seeds at a time; extra items queue
300 requests per minute per API token; 60 per hour for uncached torrent creation
3 active downloads at once; further additions queue; the global maximum is 10 slots

limits_note: Any download showing no progress for two days is removed automatically, and the maximum active-slot count across all plans is 10.
binding_note: Downloads are unlimited, so the monthly total does not bind; what fails is a single object over 200 GB. A 1 TiB month made of 200 GB items is fine on this plan, and a 1 TiB single torrent is not.

identity_cost.detail: E-mail account plus a card or voucher at checkout.

reliability_note: Usenet is not on this plan according to the vendor's support article even though the pricing page's feature column lists it for every tier; treat usenet as Pro-only. The terms allow throttling and key rotation on suspected sharing.
confidence_note: Plan limits from the pricing page; the usenet conflict is resolved conservatively against the plan's own feature column. Confirming it needs a purchase.

evidence.proved: '$3/mo', '3 Concurrent Slots', 'Unlimited Downloads', '200GB Max Per Download Size', '1Gbps Speed', '24 Hour Seeding Time', '300GB Permanent Storage'
Essential: '3 Active downloads', '200GB max torrent size', 'Access to web downloads', 'No access to Usenet downloads'
300/min per token, 60/hour for uncached torrent creation, and the per-plan download-size error table giving 214748364800 bytes for Essential
Essential: '3 Active downloads', '200GB max torrent size', 'Unlimited monthly downloads', 'Access to web downloads', no Usenet
'Essential: 300GB' Airlock and the 30-day inactivity deletion for normal files

notes: Two vendor pages disagree on usenet for this tier and the record keeps the smaller claim. The 2025 promotional listings for annual plans imply an annual list price near US$33 (US$23.10 at 30% off), but the pricing page read today shows monthly billing only, so no annual figure is recorded. The price that actually answers the 20 GiB question: USD 3 buys a 200 GB single-torrent ceiling and 300 GB of permanent storage. At 1 TiB a month it costs 3 dollars; the same terabyte on Seedr Basic costs 7.95 and on put.io 9.99.

extras.usenet: no, per the support article (the pricing page lists it for all tiers)
extras.annual_plan: exists; list price not shown on the page read, promo implies about USD 33
extras.seeding_stated: not stated for Essential; Standard is 2 weeks, Pro is 30 days
